summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of hypertension, migraines, diabetes, and a VP shunt presented with headache, chest pain, and palpitations. Initial concern for aortic dissection prompted a CT angiogram, which ruled out dissection and pulmonary embolism but revealed a small hiatal hernia. Her symptoms were attributed to elevated blood pressure, migraine, and possible reflux. Blood pressure was stabilized, and symptoms improved during the hospitalization. She was counseled on CPAP use for sleep apnea and smoking cessation. Her diabetes remained well-controlled on oral medication. She was discharged home with follow-up plans and education on symptom monitoring.
